rows.source_ref: EMA Spinraza (nusinersen) EPAR public assessment report, EMA/289068/2017 (EMEA/H/C/004312)
rows.notes: ADJACENT-HAEMATOLOGY FALLBACK ROW (is_platelet_specific FALSE): haematology was monitored and reported as showing no trends, but platelets are not itemised at that locus. The same EPAR states (section 3.5) that 'Thrombocytopenia and coagulation abnormalities, including acute severe thrombocytopenia, have been observed after administration of OTHER subcutaneously or intravenously administered antisense oligonucleotides' and that 'To date, there is no evidence in the nusinersen nonclinical and clinical safety data to suggest a signal for these toxicities' - the SmPC warning is an explicitly precautionary CLASS-EFFECT warning, not a nusinersen finding. Thrombocytopenia is listed in the RMP as an 'important potential risk', never an identified risk.

rows.effect_vs_control: 1 mild transient thrombocytopenia AE on patisiran vs 1 moderate thrombocytopenia AE + 1 mild platelet-count-decreased AE on placebo
rows.source_ref: EMA Onpattro (patisiran) EPAR public assessment report, EMA/554262/2018 (EMEA/H/C/004699)
rows.notes: Graded 1 (mild, transient, no intervention). EMA text: 'Mean platelet parameters (including platelet counts and mean platelet volume) were also stable in both the patisiran-LNP and placebo groups throughout the course of the study. No patients had platelet counts <50 x10^9/L (CTCAE Grade 3).' The only <75 x10^9/L value in the trial was in a PLACEBO subject. EMA explicitly framed this against the ASO class expectation ('The non-clinical and clinical experience so far with therapeutic oligonucleotides (mainly of the ASO (DNA-based) class) has shown that these may affect haematology values due to immune stimulation').

rows.exposure_duration: 18 months (0.3 mg/kg IV q3wk, APOLLO / study ALN-TTR02-004)
rows.effect_vs_control: no patient had a platelet count <50 x10^9/L; lowest observed value 72 x10^9/L in a subject whose baseline was already 73 x10^9/L
rows.source_table: Clinical review p.147, section 8.4.6 Laboratory Findings, 'Platelets' narrative (with Tables 67 and 68)
rows.notes: MEASURED GRADE 0. Mean MINIMUM change from baseline (Table 68) was -11 x10^9/L on patisiran vs -23 x10^9/L on placebo, i.e. the drug arm fell LESS than placebo. Mean MAXIMUM change (Table 67) was +15 vs +1.3, driven entirely by one outlier with reactive thrombocytosis during a pneumonia/SIRS hospitalisation.

rows.exposure_duration: 3 loading doses then monthly (study 101 Part C, 28 weeks + OLE)
rows.effect_vs_control: 'no difference in platelet counts over time between the placebo and tofersen-treated participants'; no AEs of thrombocytopenia and no sustained or severe thrombocytopenia in the whole clinical development programme
rows.source_ref: EMA Qalsody (tofersen) EPAR public assessment report, EMA/276404/2024 (EMEA/H/C/006072)
rows.notes: MEASURED GRADE 0 and the most informative ASO negative control here: tofersen is a 2'-MOE gapmer with a real (if partial) PS backbone - 15 of 19 linkages are phosphorothioate per the FDA label - yet delivered INTRATHECALLY it produces no platelet signal. Supports systemic plasma exposure, not PS chemistry alone, as the driver. Proportion shifting from normal/high to low platelet count was similar in tofersen and placebo.

rows.effect_vs_control: 2 participants had a single platelet value <100 x10^9/L; both had a repeat result showing normal counts, no bleeding, none reported as an AE
rows.source_ref: EMA Qalsody (tofersen) EPAR public assessment report, EMA/276404/2024 (EMEA/H/C/006072)
rows.notes: Graded 2 strictly on the numeric band (<100 x10^9/L falls outside the grade-1 '>=100' band), but the events were transient, self-resolving, non-adverse and required no intervention - the practical severity is closer to grade 1. Recorded here so the numeric band is not lost.

rows.effect_vs_control: 6 participants (4.1%) had a shift to a low platelet count; proportion similar to placebo
rows.source_ref: EMA Qalsody (tofersen) EPAR public assessment report, EMA/276404/2024 (EMEA/H/C/006072)
rows.notes: Graded 1: laboratory shifts to 'low' without any AE, intervention or bleeding, and at a rate similar to placebo.
